steps.plantedFailures: Blocking work: the planted login hashes on the main thread, which now and then holds a request past k6's timeout (1 of about 144 in most repeats on CI).

note: Load form (research/load-harness.md) for L09: a cheap request (an avatar, about 1 ms) at 20 a second while a second scenario sends one route at a time at its own rate. Work on the main thread holds up every other request; work off it does not. For login and export the judged quantity is the share of avatar requests not answered within 100 ms; a twin reports at three times the other's share and at least 30%. Signup is judged on the event loop's longest stretch over the step (monitorEventLoopDelay), at three times the other twin's and at least 50 ms, with signups at 2 a second: at 8 a second the hashing filled both CPUs in the clean twin too, off the main thread, so its avatars were as late as the planted twin's (CI run 44609939663; the owner, 19 November 2026). The one-time codes hash with bcryptjs at cost 4 in both twins: the decoy. Each step runs at a fixed arrival rate (k6), each twin judged against the other over 5 pairs in alternating order, every finding under the relative timing rule (all five pairs, none, or a mix: unreliable). defects are what the planted twin must report and the clean twin must not; every other judged step is a decoy, in both twins. GET /export (the owner, 20 November 2026): both twins make the export's JSON, encoded to bytes, and its ETag when the orders change, so a request only compresses (gzipSync on the request path in the planted twin; in the clean twin a worker thread that compresses and returns one buffer, since zlib.gzip's output, handed back to the main thread in 16 KiB chunks, cost the main thread allocations and garbage collections: 31 to 37 ms an export on a Mac, 105 ms on CI). The export holds 1,000,000 orders ("env" L09_ORDERS; the trace form seeds 200,000), about 100 MB of JSON, sent at 2 a second: gzipSync then holds the planted twin's loop about 445 ms an export on a Mac, well past the 100 ms an avatar may wait, where 200,000 orders at 6 a second held it about 89 ms and the planted twin's late share fell to 0.08 to 0.13 (CI run 44725479816). Fixture targets: the planted twin's late share at least 0.6 in every pair (the bar stays 0.3 and 3x); the clean twin's at most 0.05, its main thread busy at most 0.05 at this rate on a Mac. Acceptance condition (cleanMax): the clean twin's late share on this step is at most 0.05 in every pair of every run, and the planted twin clears 3 times in every pair; CI run 44682458078, before the change, had the clean twin at 0.46 to 0.53, its own JSON and hash holding the main thread 90 to 136 ms a request.
